narrative:
The model estimates a 63% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional profile that, according to patterns seen across many similar employees, tend to signal higher turnover risk.

Most influential was your total years of experience. With 6–10 years overall, you sit in a range where people are noticeably more likely to move on compared with the majority of those predicted to stay, who tend to have only 1–5 years of total experience. This factor pushed the prediction toward leaving.

The second strongest influence was the length of time you have spent in your current organization. At 1–5 years, this is actually the most common range among employees the model expects to stay. In your case, however, the combination with your broader career stage made the model interpret it as part of a pattern that still leans toward departure rather than long-term retention.

Third, the model noted that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities is relatively uncommon among those predicted to stay (only about 23% of that group report receiving them). This factor also pulled the prediction toward leaving.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed many positive signals such as your high salary, strong recognition, and satisfaction with training. The organization should discuss retention options with you soon, while you may wish to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term career goals. (248 words)
